messages.content: write a story about a child who waits at the wrong door before a school trip. make someone help by asking a question.

a child stood near the front door of the school with a container of food for the trip. the other children were not there yet. a teacher came through the room and asked which group the child was waiting for. the child said they were going to the library. the teacher said that group was meeting at the door near the garden. they walked there together. when the child saw the group, she asked why they were using that door. the teacher said it was the one near the vehicle they would take.
can you give the conversation with the teacher, without all the story around it?
which group are you waiting for? the group going to the library. they are meeting at the door near the garden. would you like me to show you? yes, please. i thought we were using the front door.
why was the question better than just telling the child to go outside?
the teacher needed to know which group the child wanted. outside alone would not say which door or where the right group was.
what did the child get right before the teacher came?
the child was at the school with food for the trip. she knew the group was going to the library. the part that needed changing was where she was waiting.
add a short part at the end where she thinks about what to ask next time.
the child put her food with the other things for the trip. next time, she thought, i will ask where the group is meeting before i choose a door.
my friend asked about a book i finished. i want to tell them why i liked it without telling them what happens at the end.
you can talk about the kind of story, the people in it, or how you felt while reading. leave out the choice or change at the end if your friend wants to find that out by reading.
it is about a young person who leaves home and learns to work in a new town. i liked the small details about making friends.
then you could say: it is about someone making a new life in another town. i liked how the story showed the small things that helped people become friends.
my friend asked whether the person goes home. i do not know if they want the answer or are just asking about the idea.
you can check before giving that part away: do you want me to tell you, or would you rather find out when you read it?
they say they would rather read it. what can i say next?
you can return to a part that does not answer the question. for example: then i will leave that for you to find out. i would like to hear what you think after you read it.
should i say it is the best book they will read in their whole life?
you can say you enjoyed it without choosing how they will feel. people can like different books. a specific reason you liked it gives your friend more information than saying they must like it best.
keep the last answer simple.
say why you liked it, and let your friend find out whether they like it too.
i looked at the clock before a phone call. it was two. after the call, it was three. can i say the call took one hour?

if the clock was right and you started the call at two and finished at three, then it took one hour. if you waited before starting or looked at the clock long after finishing, you would need to know more.
i started as the clock showed two and finished as it showed three. the clock was working well.
then in your example the call took one hour, from two to three.
i read for another hour after that. when did i finish reading?
if you started reading at three and read for one hour, you finished at four.
what if i had a ten minute rest before reading?
then reading started ten minutes after three. after an hour of reading, it would be ten minutes after four.
write the whole order using words only.
the call went from two to three. then you had a rest for ten minutes. after that, you read for one hour and finished ten minutes after four.
did i read for more than one hour because the end was after four?
no. the reading still took one hour. the rest made it start later, so it also finished later. the time between the call and the end of reading was an hour and ten minutes.
can you ask me one question about that order?
what did you do after the call but before you started reading?
i want to learn a song my father used to sing. i remember the sound, but not all the words. i thought i would know them because i have heard the song again and again.
you can remember one part well and still need help with another. knowing the sound does not always mean you can bring every word to mind. do you have a way to hear the song again?
my sister has it on her phone. she said i can listen with her.
then you could listen to a short part, stop, and try the words you heard. after that, listen again to check. one line at a time may be enough to start.
i do not want to spend the whole evening doing it.
you can choose just one part for today. learning a little does not have to become a task that takes all your free time.
what can i ask my sister?
could we listen to one short part of the song together? i want to learn the words, and i might need to hear it more than once.
what if the words she knows sound different from the words on the phone?

you can listen together and talk about what each of you heard. people sometimes sing the same song with some different words, so one difference does not tell you that someone remembered everything wrong.
say that simply.
people can sing the same song with some different words. listen together and see which words are in the one on the phone.
i am visiting a friend. i want to move a chair near the window so i can read in the light. how can i ask without making it sound like their room is wrong?
you can ask about moving the chair for your own use, rather than saying the room should be different. for example: would it be okay if i moved this chair near the window while i read?
i can put it back before i leave. add that.
would it be okay if i moved this chair near the window while i read? i can put it back before i leave.
my friend says the chair has a broken leg. they want me to use another one.
then use the other chair if that works for you. the answer gives a reason about this chair, rather than saying you cannot read near the window at all.
should i still move the broken chair out of the way?
ask before moving it. your friend may have a place they want it kept, and you do not need to move it just because you are using another chair.
write a short reply asking about the other chair.
thank you for telling me. could i put the other chair near the window instead?
they say yes. what should i remember at the end of the visit?
you said you could put the chair back before leaving. if that is still what your friend wants, return it to its place when you finish reading.
write a story about a grandmother getting a drawing and a letter from a boy in her family. have her answer with a question about the picture.

a grandmother found a letter near her door. inside was a drawing of a garden and a short message from a boy in her family. he wrote that he had been thinking about the garden at her house. she looked at the trees and saw a small chair under one of them. in her reply, she said thank you and asked whether the chair was the place where they had sat together last year. he wrote back that it was, and that he remembered listening to her stories there.
make the reply from the grandmother sound like a real message.
thank you for the drawing. i like seeing the garden through your eyes. is the chair under the tree the one where we sat together last year?
what does through your eyes mean here?
it is about seeing how he chose to draw the garden and what parts he remembered. it is his way of looking at the place, rather than using his real eyes.
make that explanation shorter.
it is about his way of looking at the garden. the drawing can show what he remembered and wanted to put on the page.
now give his short answer to her question.
yes, that is the chair. i remember sitting there while you told me stories.
did the first letter already say all that about the chair?
no. the first letter said he was thinking about the garden. the question and his answer added the specific memory about sitting together under the tree.
i am writing a note for my brother and me. should i say i will clean the kitchen if we are both doing it?
if the note is about both of you doing the work, we will clean the kitchen makes that clear. i will clean the kitchen gives the task to you alone unless you add more information.
we are both cleaning, but he will wash the cups and i will clean the table. write that.
we will clean the kitchen. my brother will wash the cups, and i will clean the table.
this note is for him too. can i write you instead of my brother?
yes. if the note speaks to him, you can say: we will clean the kitchen. you can wash the cups, and i will clean the table.
is you can the same as you will?
not always. you can may sound like a choice or something possible. you will says what is going to happen in the plan. if you have both chosen the work already, you will can keep that clear.
we already chose it. give me that note.
we will clean the kitchen. you will wash the cups, and i will clean the table.
now write it as a question before we have chosen.
shall we clean the kitchen together? would you like to wash the cups while i clean the table?
why change the words rather than only ask will we clean the kitchen?
will we clean the kitchen asks whether it will happen. would you like to wash the cups asks what part the other person wants to do. the note about a plan says what both people have already chosen.
hi picoboi. i am not sure what to talk about.
hello. we can start with something simple. would you like to talk about your day, ask a question, or make up a short story together?
ask me about my day, but not many questions at once.
what is one thing you did today?
i went to the library and sat by the window. i did not read much, but i liked being there.
that sounds like a quiet part of your day. was it the place by the window that you liked, or something else about being there?
i liked seeing people walk outside while i sat with a book. i did not feel like i had to finish it.
then the book was part of having a calm place to sit, rather than a task you needed to finish. you can enjoy time with a book even if you only read a little.
can you write a small story from that idea? make the person different from me.

a woman took a book to the library and found a chair near the window. she read one page, then watched people walking outside. after a while, she put a hand between the pages and looked at the sky. she had come to read, but she was happy to sit quietly too. when she left, she had not finished the book. she still felt the afternoon had been good.
why did you make it a woman?
you asked for someone different from you, so i chose a person for the made up story. that choice is part of the story, not new information about who you are.
